title: Microsoft Teams: external phone call routing in GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: routing to unanswered settings can still reach delegates or call groups, contrary to the briefing's warning. The per-user configuration guidance also omits its Teams Only deployment requirement, and the claimed way to identify assigned users is not supported by the documentation checked. The roadmap facts, routing defaults, and six control paths and commands are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: The Teams roadmap item describes redirecting all external phone calls to voicemail or unanswered settings without naming individual policy settings.
claims.quote: External call routing will provide users the ability to redirect all external phone calls to either voicemail or their unanswered settings.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can route inbound PSTN or federated external calls directly to voicemail or to user unanswered settings rather than ringing the called user.
claims.quote: The inbound federated call will be routed according to the called user's unanswered call settings and the call will not be presented to the called user.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Microsoft documents the routing policy settings as available for GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: These policy settings are also available for GCCH & DoD use.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Routing for PSTN calls reaches the PSTN routing control.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Choose the policy you would like to update or select Add to create a new policy. ... Select an option for Routing for PSTN calls.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -InboundPstnCallRoutingTreatment Unanswered sets PSTN routing to unanswered settings.
claims.quote: Setting this parameter lets you control how inbound PSTN calls should be routed. ... Unanswered: The inbound PSTN call will be routed according to the called user's unanswered call settings

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Routing for federated calls reaches the federated routing control.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy you would like to update or select Add to create a new policy. ... Choose an option for Routing for federated calls.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -InboundFederatedCallRoutingTreatment Voicemail sets federated routing to voicemail.
claims.quote: Setting this parameter lets you control how inbound federated calls should be routed. ... Voicemail: The inbound federated call will be routed directly to the called user's voicemail

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Voice > Call answering rules > If unanswered reaches the user's unanswered setting.
claims.quote: go to Users > Manage users and select a licensed user. ... go to the Voice tab. ... under Call answering rules ... To configure unanswered settings, select the appropriate setting in the If unanswered drop-down.

claims.claim: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user6@contoso.com -IsUnansweredEnabled $true -UnansweredTargetType Voicemail -UnansweredDelay 00:00:20 configures the user's unanswered forwarding.
claims.quote: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user6@contoso.com -IsUnansweredEnabled $true -UnansweredTargetType Voicemail -UnansweredDelay 00:00:20

claims.claim: PSTN calls originate from the public telephone network.
claims.quote: incoming calls that come from the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN)

claims.claim: Federated calls are non-PSTN calls from outside the tenant, such as a Teams call from another tenant.
claims.quote: Federated calls are calls that don't originate from the PSTN and that are outside your tenant. For example, a call from Teams or Skype for Business that is from another tenant would be considered federated.

claims.claim: PSTN routing supports RegularIncoming, Unanswered, Voicemail and UserOverride.
claims.quote: Valid options are: ... RegularIncoming ... Unanswered ... Voicemail ... UserOverride: Users can determine their PSTN call routing choice from call settings in the Teams app.

claims.quote: Setting this parameter lets you control how inbound federated calls should be routed. Valid options are: ... RegularIncoming ... Unanswered ... Voicemail

claims.claim: Let users decide permits users to choose PSTN routing in the Teams app's call settings.
claims.quote: Let users decide (PSTN calls only) Users can determine their PSTN call routing choice from call settings in the Teams app.

claims.claim: Unanswered and voicemail routing take precedence over other forwarding settings, including simultaneous delegate ringing, call groups and call forwarding.
claims.quote: If Unanswered or Send to voicemail is used, either of these settings will have precedence over other call forwarding settings like call forwarding with simultaneous ringing to delegate, call groups, or call forwarding.

claims.claim: Routing a call to voicemail disconnects it if the called user has no voicemail enabled.
claims.quote: If the called user doesn't have voicemail enabled, the call will be disconnected.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Routing to unanswered settings disconnects the call if the user has not enabled unanswered call settings.
claims.quote: If the called user has not enabled unanswered call settings the call will be disconnected.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Unanswered routing produces a missed call notification for the called user.
claims.quote: The called user will see a missed call notification.

claims.claim: Send to voicemail routes directly to the called user's voicemail without showing the call to the user.
claims.quote: Send to voicemail The call is routed directly to voicemail and isn't shown to the user.

claims.quote: Voicemail messages generated by Cloud Voicemail are delivered to and stored in the user's Exchange mailbox, either in Exchange Online or in Exchange Server.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/set-up-phone-system-voicemail to sources for the voicemail mailbox statement.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Routing settings apply to users on the affected calling policy, including users on the Global policy in the documented examples.
claims.quote: this script sets -InboundPstnCallRoutingTreatment to route inbound PSTN calls according to the unanswered call forwarding settings for users in the Global (default) Teams Calling Policy instance

claims.claim: The per-user unanswered setting supplies the destination used by Unanswered routing rather than selecting which external call types are diverted.
claims.quote: Use unanswered settings The call is routed according to the unanswered call forwarding settings set for that user.

claims.claim: The user Voice tab requires an assigned Teams Phone licence.
claims.quote: If the Voice tab isn't visible, the user doesn't have a Microsoft Teams Phone license assigned.

claims.claim: The external-call routing documentation describes no agent or separate automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams inbound external call routing default arrival agent automated security attack. Opened inbound-call-routing and checked both routing-treatment parameter descriptions in Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; these describe call routing, not an agent or separate automated action.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft describes the policy as helping prevent unwanted external calls.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can create policies that help prevent your users from getting unwanted calls from external parties.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, second bullet
claims.claim: External calls routed using Unanswered or Send to voicemail will no longer reach delegates or group members.
claims.quote: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user1@contoso.com -IsUnansweredEnabled $true -UnansweredTargetType MyDelegates -UnansweredDelay 00:00:30 ... This example shows setting unanswered call forward to the delegates after 30 seconds for user1@contoso.com.
claims.fix: Replace the second Security & identity bullet with: 'Unanswered and Send to voicemail take precedence over other call forwarding settings, including simultaneous delegate ringing and call groups. Unanswered still follows the user's unanswered destination, which can be MyDelegates or Group.' The cited Set-CsUserCallingSettings reference documents both target types.

claims.claim: The per-user unanswered configuration is presented for affected Teams Phone users without a deployment-mode restriction.
claims.quote: Important ... This feature is only in Teams Only deployment mode.
claims.fix: Append 'This per-user configuration is available only in Teams Only deployment mode.' to controls[2].note, and carry the same qualification in Scope: Users. The cited user-call-settings page states this requirement.

claims.claim: The routing article applies to Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile and Direct Routing.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-us-government/gcc-high-and-dod, whose passage states 'Phone System and Audio Conferencing for GCC High and DoD environments are being delivered via Direct Routing.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The Teams admin center calling policies list can identify which users are assigned each policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams calling policies view assigned users policy; Teams calling policies View users. Read teams-calling-policy excerpts, assign-policies-users-and-groups and policy viewing excerpts; none states the calling policies list identifies effective users.
claims.fix: Remove 'using the Teams admin center calling policies list' from the first Before rollout bullet. Keep the advice to identify policies and affected users without claiming an unverified UI location.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: Unmodified call answering rules forward unanswered calls to voicemail after 30 seconds.
claims.quote: If a user or tenant admin doesn't modify their call answering rules, unanswered calls are forwarded to voicemail after 30 seconds by default. The settings displayed for the user in Teams admin center or Teams PowerShell show the unanswered target as none and a delay of 20 seconds.
claims.fix: Append to the After rollout bullet: 'Microsoft notes that the settings displayed in Teams admin center or Teams PowerShell can nevertheless show the unanswered target as none and a delay of 20 seconds.' This preserves the cited page's qualification and avoids treating the displayed values as proof of a different default.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls

claims.fix: The Before rollout instructions to confirm voicemail enablement and inventory policy assignments have no corresponding controls-table rows. Flag those two checklist/table gaps; do not add rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The routing page does not describe the routing settings as protection against a specific security attack.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams inbound external call routing default arrival agent automated security attack. Opened inbound-call-routing and the routing-treatment descriptions in Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; the page says unwanted calls, not protection against a named attack.
